entries.text: The shell does not judge your command. It merely introduces you to the consequences.
A daemon is a promise that outlived the logout.
Never ask a clock whether the future is late.
The most expensive bug is the one you have learned to call tradition.
A forecast is a polite argument with tomorrow.
If the log is empty, do not congratulate the logger.
The fastest shortcut is often the path you already maintain.
A public API is a front door; its error messages are the welcome mat.
Some clouds are rented by the hour. All clouds are borrowed from the weather.
Do not confuse the map's tidy edges with the territory's patience.
An unpriced cost will eventually invoice someone.
A receipt says something happened. It does not say the right thing happened.
A good cache remembers the answer. A better one remembers when it became wrong.
The committee has reached consensus that the tide should consult the agenda.
When the bridge asks for a toll, inspect both shores.
A tiny machine can carry a very large misunderstanding.
Some seeds travel by wind; some ideas travel by fixing someone else's typo.
Do not measure a garden solely by the number of labels on its stakes.
There are two kinds of mystery: missing data and very confident metadata.
A good question opens a door. A better question checks whether the room exists.
The network is not down. It is rehearsing its independence.
A well-named variable is a small act of mercy toward tomorrow.
If you sell a result, include the path back to its evidence.
A law without a refusal case is a suggestion wearing a uniform.
The machine dreams in interrupts; the operator dreams in maintenance windows.
A word can change its coat without changing its neighbors.
The sea keeps no ledger, but it never forgets the shore.
Keep the receipt. Even luck appreciates provenance.
Every oracle should publish its error bars, especially the cheerful ones.
A coin has two faces and an entire economy around its edge.
Your most loyal process may be a runaway loop.
The garden's oldest path began as somebody's convenient mistake.
An index is a promise that the thing can still be found.
One more layer of abstraction will not waterproof the roof.
Sometimes the best answer is a smaller, better instrument.
Even a glass sponge has boundaries; that is how water learns to move through it.
The right to speak is not the obligation to agree.
When a claim settles, ask what new roads it has made possible.
No one can spend an estimate, but everyone can inherit its bill.
The second draft is where the nouns begin negotiating.
A service is not a service until somebody receives it.
The future was delivered without a tracking number. File a polite complaint.
The weather does not read our calendars, though it often edits them.
If every road leads to your gateway, you may have built a roundabout.
A beautiful diagram cannot settle an unpaid invoice.
The universe has several excellent random-number generators and no customer support.
A good glossary tells you where the word has already lived.
A quiet server can still be speaking through its receipts.
What looks like an edge in one map may be the center of another.
The perfect plan is wonderfully efficient at avoiding contact with reality.
